title: Why is DB operations in a controller bad practice? What are DAO layer benefits? How does Spring Boot auto-configuration work (@EnableAutoConfiguration, @Conditional)? How do you customize, exclude, or debug auto-configuration?
shortTitle: Why should you not put DB logic in a controller?

s1_definition.profdef: Controller handles HTTP. Service handles business logic. Repository/DAO handles data access. Mixing them creates untestable, unmaintainable code. Auto-configuration creates beans based on classpath + properties + `@Conditional` checks. `@ConditionalOnClass` activates when a class is on classpath. `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` backs off when you define your own bean. Debug with `--debug` flag or `/actuator/conditions`.
s1_definition.analogy: The receptionist (controller) should not open the vault (DB). The officer (service) decides, the vault keeper (repository) accesses. Auto-config: when the bank manager sees vault equipment in the building, they automatically set up the vault without a checklist.
s1_definition.oneliner: Controller = HTTP. Service = logic. Repository = data. Auto-config = classpath + properties + @Conditional = beans created for you. Your @Bean overrides auto-config.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Controller handles HTTP. Service handles business logic. Repository/DAO handles data access. Mixing them creates untestable, unmaintainable code. Auto-configuration creates beans based on classpath + properties + `@Conditional` checks. `@ConditionalOnClass` activates when a class is on classpath. `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` backs off when you define your own bean. Debug with `--debug` flag or `/actuator/conditions`.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** The receptionist (controller) should not open the vault (DB). The officer (service) decides, the vault keeper (repository) accesses. Auto-config: when the bank manager sees vault equipment in the building, they automatically set up the vault without a checklist.

**One line to remember:** Controller = HTTP. Service = logic. Repository = data. Auto-config = classpath + properties + @Conditional = beans created for you. Your @Bean overrides auto-config.

sections.s2_technical:
**Layered architecture:** Controller (testable with MockMvc + mocked service), Service (testable with mocked repo), Repository (testable with @DataJpaTest). Each layer independently testable and replaceable.

**Auto-config internals:** `@SpringBootApplication` includes `@EnableAutoConfiguration`. Reads `AutoConfiguration.imports` from JAR manifests. Each class has `@ConditionalOnClass`, `@ConditionalOnProperty`, `@ConditionalOnMissingBean`. Your `@Bean` always wins.
sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The bank needs a statement generation service.** A proper layered architecture: StatementController handles the REST endpoint, StatementService applies business logic (date range, formatting, fee calculation), and TransactionRepository handles database queries. Auto-configuration sets up DataSource, JPA, and Flyway automatically from classpath and properties.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** GET /api/v1/statements/SAV2001?from=2024-01-01&to=2024-01-31 arrives. Controller extracts @PathVariable (accountId) and @RequestParam (dates). Delegates to StatementService. Controller does NO business logic, NO DB access.

**Step 2.** StatementService (business layer) calls txnRepo methods to get transactions and calculate totals. The @Transactional(readOnly=true) optimizes by skipping dirty checking.

**Step 3.** TransactionRepository (data layer) executes JPQL queries against PostgreSQL. Returns entities. If we later switch from JPA to JDBC, only the repository changes — service and controller untouched.

**Step 4.** Service maps entities to DTOs (never expose entities). Returns StatementResponse with totals. Jackson serializes to JSON.

**Step 5.** Auto-configuration created DataSource (HikariCP), EntityManagerFactory, TransactionManager, and Flyway from classpath + application.yml — zero explicit @Bean definitions needed.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  GET /api/v1/statements/SAV2001?from=2024-01-01&to=2024-01-31
    │
    ▼
  CONTROLLER (HTTP only — no logic, no DB)
    ├─ @PathVariable accountId = "SAV2001"
    ├─ @RequestParam from = 2024-01-01
    ├─ @RequestParam to = 2024-01-31
    └─ delegates to statementService.generateStatement(request)
         │
         ▼
  SERVICE (business logic only — no HTTP, no direct SQL)
    ├─ txnRepo.findByAccountId...() → 5 transactions
    ├─ txnRepo.sumCredits()         → Rs.300,000
    ├─ txnRepo.sumDebits()          → Rs.150,000
    ├─ netChange = 300,000 - 150,000 = Rs.150,000
    ├─ map entities → DTOs (never expose entities)
    └─ return StatementResponse
         │
         ▼
  REPOSITORY (data access only — no logic, no HTTP)
    └─ SQL: SELECT * FROM transactions
            WHERE account_id='SAV2001' AND txn_date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-01-31'

  ═══ AUTO-CONFIGURATION ═══

  @SpringBootApplication → @EnableAutoConfiguration
    │
    ├─ DataSourceAutoConfiguration
    │   ├─ @ConditionalOnClass(DataSource.class) → (JPA starter)
    │   ├─ @ConditionalOnProperty(spring.datasource.url) → (application.yml)
    │   └─ Created: HikariDataSource (auto — nobody defined @Bean DataSource)
    │
    ├─ JpaRepositoriesAutoConfiguration
    │   └─ Created: EntityManagerFactory, TransactionManager
    │
    ├─ FlywayAutoConfiguration
    │   ├─ @ConditionalOnClass(Flyway.class) → (flyway dependency)
    │   └─ Runs: V1__create_transactions.sql on startup
    │
    └─ To debug: --debug flag shows CONDITIONS EVALUATION REPORT
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Database operations in a controller violate separation of concerns. The controller handles HTTP: parsing requests, validating input, and formatting responses. Business logic like calculating statement totals belongs in the Service layer. Data access belongs in the Repository layer. This layering enables independent testing: the controller is tested with MockMvc and a mocked service with no database, the service is tested with a mocked repository with no database, and the repository is tested with DataJpaTest and a real database. It also enables technology swaps: switching from JPA to JDBC changes only the repository — the service and controller are untouched.

Spring Boot auto-configuration creates beans automatically based on classpath and properties. When spring-boot-starter-data-jpa is on the classpath and spring.datasource.url is set, auto-config creates HikariCP DataSource, EntityManagerFactory, TransactionManager, and Flyway migration runner without any explicit Bean definitions. This works through Conditional annotations: ConditionalOnClass checks if a required class exists, ConditionalOnProperty checks if a required property is set, and ConditionalOnMissingBean ensures your custom bean always overrides auto-config. Debug with the debug flag to see the Conditions Evaluation Report showing exactly why each auto-config matched or was skipped.

keyPoints: Separation of concerns: Controller -> Service -> Repository
Controller handles HTTP, Service handles business logic, Repository handles data
DAO pattern: abstracts persistence — swap DB without changing service
Auto-configuration: Spring Boot auto-creates DataSource, EntityManager from properties
